AC: SKILL.md (and tool where mechanical) cover: router fields, mechanical level-triggered orchestrator loop, acceptance gate before done, escalation with retry bound and explicit wreckage policy, worker exit contract, and the ephemeral episodic memory layer; doctor stays ok; ALT:easy fields land unchanged as phase 1.

Body.raw:
ALTERNATIVE (full cascade routing) design. Original todo: 557ab9d3. Minimal
counterpart: ALT:easy, todo 5774cf41 (5774cf4107ea07d652a8c87069f188d356f548cf9c9338b2f2e459cf1a9caadf) -- it is phase 1 of this design
(the router fields) and remains valid as a subset.

Design (chat discussion 2026-07-17/18):

1. Router (= ALT:easy 5774cf41): groomed execution.capability / execution.effort
   on WorkItems/subtodos set the STARTING tier; absent = inherit.

2. Orchestrator: one cheap agent (haiku/sonnet) per parent todo. Purely mechanical:
   polls work-item-read / wait-for, follows next hints, dispatches workers; never
   authors content. Judgment operations (splitting, grooming, merge-conflict
   resolution, parent synthesis) are dispatched as work items to capable tiers,
   not done inline by the orchestrator.
   Level-triggered: on ANY wake (harness completion notification, poll timeout,
   manual poke) it recomputes the frontier from the store (ls -t, Subtodos states,
   work-item-read) rather than trusting remembered launches. Wake channels are
   latency optimizations only; the orchestrator is restartable-stateless.

3. Acceptance gate: a work item / subtodo is done only when its AC / test gate
   passes, checked mechanically -- never worker self-report.

4. Escalation (the cascade half): on gate failure, re-dispatch the SAME item at
   the next tier up (sonnet -> opus -> fable), bounded retries, then userneeded.
   Wreckage policy is explicit in the escalated prompt: continue from the failed
   attempt's commits, or reset to BaseSha / last good work-item sha.

5. Worker exit contract (durable correctness floor): workers run fresh-context;
   before exit, everything needed for correctness lands in durable stores --
   commits with full -m messages, work-item-done message, ActualSummary. These
   have mechanical consumers (merge-subtodo commit subject, escalation prompt,
   observability) and must survive loss of any cache.

6. Episodic memory (recall tail, ephemeral): embedding index (redis or similar)
   over worker session transcripts for read-time retrieval; optionally include
   session n-1 verbatim in prompt n (one hop, recency continuity). Explicitly
   ephemeral: losing it must never break resumption -- the git+todo ledger stays
   the correctness floor. Caution: do not feed a FAILED session verbatim to the
   escalated worker (anchoring / context poisoning); escalation prefers the
   distilled attempt summary plus targeted retrieval.

7. Prompt assembly (orchestrator): todo prompt (WHY chain) + WHAT-state resume
   info (files touched, last-sha, failing test output; a prompt --resume style
   extension) + skill insertion + episodic retrieval hits.

8. Per-todo static skill index (TodoMemory) -- the CHEAP tier of #7's "skill
   insertion", distinct from #6's embedding recall. A per-todo (per-branch) file
   holds a small table of `trigger/description -> linked reference` plus an
   explicit instruction: "when a trigger matches the work, read the linked
   reference." The orchestrator injects this table into the fresh worker's
   startup prompt (via prompt / work-item-read next hint), giving tailored,
   pruned context without a long-lived session. Modeled on Claude Code auto-memory,
   whose verified mechanics are: the MEMORY.md index is loaded WHOLESALE at session
   start (first 200 lines / 25KB), and bodies are READ ON DEMAND by the agent (Read
   tool) -- there is NO harness-side associative/embedding recall of bodies.
   Consequence: the trigger match is AGENT-EVALUATED, not automatic, and the table
   is resident context every turn -- so keep it small and pointer-only (bodies live
   in the linked refs, pulled only on match). True relevance-gated retrieval (pay
   only when relevant) is #6's embedding tier / `todo search`, layered on top when
   wanted. (Ref: code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents, "Enable persistent memory".)

9. Lean-vs-capable tension + resolution (chat 2026-07-20). CONCERN: pre-selecting
   skills for a fresh worker risks a cheap selector omitting reasoning-relevant
   knowledge, putting blinders on the hi-cap agent; but making the selector as
   capable as the worker appears to save nothing. RESOLUTION: selection and solving
   are different-cost tasks, and RETRIEVAL IS A PRIOR, NOT A GATE -- the cheap tier
   proposes, the capable tier disposes (and can re-retrieve).
   - What is saved is the WORKER's resident context across turns (retrieval is O(1)
     per dispatch vs O(turns) carrying the whole stable), NOT selector reasoning --
     so a moderately capable orchestrator still wins; selection is one-shot, solving
     is the long tail.
   - Curation is also a QUALITY lever, not just cost: a hi-cap agent drowning in ~40
     skills reasons WORSE (context rot / distraction / lost-in-the-middle) than one
     given the ~3 relevant. Good curation raises signal; bad curation hurts. The axis
     to optimize is signal-to-noise, not "lean vs capable". (Anthropic context-
     engineering: smallest set of high-signal tokens.)
   - Split along the capability gradient: orchestrator does COARSE, HIGH-RECALL
     retrieval (over-include; a ~8-item menu is cheap and forgiving of embedding
     sloppiness); the worker gets the MENU (not the full stable, not one guessed
     skill) plus its OWN Read/search tools and does PRECISE selection at read-time,
     RE-RETRIEVING if the menu has a gap. A menu + search is not blinders; denying
     the worker the search tool would be. Never make the cheap selector the sole gate.
   - This is the MEMORY.md shape (#8): curated index + agent's own Read tool; the
     embedding layer only makes the index relevance-ranked instead of all-N. Judgment
     stays where the capability is; it is merely pre-warmed so the worker does not
     start cold, and expensive reasoning runs ONCE, on the task, over lean high-signal
     context.
   - Embedding caveat: vectors give good TOPICAL recall but poor REASONING-relevance
     (second-order interactions are invisible to similarity) -- hence over-retrieve at
     the cheap tier and always leave the worker able to re-retrieve. Do not trust
     similarity for precision, only for a generous first cut.
   - Indexing the current session in the orchestrator is the #6 episodic tier:
     ephemeral, must NEVER gate correctness (git + todo ledger stays the floor).

10. Context for the implementing (hi-cap) worker (chat 2026-07-20). Generalizes the
    code-review insight (review the FINAL result, not per-WorkItem, since final state
    collapses blind alleys): the SAME reason forbids feeding the worker the full prior
    workstream -- dead ends are noise AND an anchoring risk (cf #6). Separate three
    registers of "previous work":
    - WHAT is true now -> the CODEBASE. Ground truth; read ON DEMAND (worker has
      Read/search), not pre-stuffed. Terra cognita, not nova: the tree already encodes
      the collapsed, blind-alley-free result of all prior items.
    - WHY + what is DONE -> the durable LEDGER: todo prompt (WHY chain) + prior items'
      ActualSummary + commit messages. The correct default SEED; distilled by
      construction (records what was done, not what was abandoned). Already mandated by
      #5's exit contract.
    - HOW incl. dead ends -> the TRANSCRIPT. NEVER feed (review-noise + anchoring).
    RULE: feed WHAT (on demand) + WHY/DONE (distilled); NEVER HOW. The codebase is not
    terra nova because code loses (a) rationale invisible in a diff, (b) the forward
    plan (avoid a local choice that collides with WorkItem N+k) -- both live in the
    ledger. Conditional on COUPLING:
    - Independent WorkItem (disjoint region, no shared decisions; the SKILL context-
      scoped case): near-terra-nova is correct -- codebase + own AC + WHY chain only.
      Max lean-context win.
    - Coupled WorkItem: seed with distilled outcomes of JUST the coupled prior items
      (their ActualSummary + relevant commits + cross-cutting decision), not all items,
      not transcripts.
    Selecting which prior summaries are relevant is #9's machinery on the TIME axis:
    orchestrator coarse-selects (high recall), worker reads codebase + re-retrieves on
    a sensed gap. Prior-work context is a PRIOR, NOT A GATE. Self-consistent with #5:
    the exit contract exists precisely so the next worker is seeded with highlights,
    not transcript -- two ends of one pipe.

===============================================================================
APPENDIX: Review 1-10 (retrospective for next grooming session; chat 2026-07-20)
===============================================================================

Reviewer: implementing-agent parting thoughts. Not yet groomed into WorkItems.

THE SPINE (what is solid and load-bearing)
- One invariant recurs and holds the whole design together: the git+todo ledger is
  the correctness FLOOR (#5), and every other store -- episodic recall (#6), TodoMemory
  skill index (#8), prior-work seed (#10) -- is a cache/optimization that MUST NEVER
  gate correctness. "Prior, not a gate" (#9) and "ephemeral, never gates" (#6) are the
  same rule on two axes (skills, time). This is the strongest idea here; protect it.
- Restartable-stateless, level-triggered orchestrator (#2) + mechanical acceptance gate
  (#3) + escalation ratchet (#4) form a robust, testable runtime spine.

OPEN TENSIONS / QUESTIONS TO GROOM (the retrospective meat)
R1. Orchestrator capability floor is unresolved. #2 wants it CHEAP and "purely
    mechanical, never authors, dispatches judgment as work items." But #9/#10 hand it
    coarse retrieval AND coupling detection ("which prior items does N couple to").
    Coupling detection smells like judgment, not mechanism. Risk: the cheap orchestrator
    quietly needs capability, reopening #9's "then what have you saved." GROOM: is
    coupling a mechanical computation (static dep graph / file-overlap / import graph) or
    a judgment call dispatched to a capable tier? Pin this; it is the design's soft spot.
R2. #3 assumes a mechanical gate EXISTS per item. Many items (design, docs, "make it
    cleaner", refactor) have no crisp test, and #4's escalation is DEFINED in terms of
    gate failure -- undefined when there is no gate. GROOM: a gate taxonomy
    (test-gated / review-gated / judgment-gated) and how escalation behaves for
    non-test gates.
R3. #4 details are underspecified: the tier ladder (sonnet->opus->fable) hardcodes a
    model order that will go stale; the retry budget is unnamed; and the wreckage
    policy (continue-from-commits vs reset-to-base) is itself a judgment call -- WHO
    makes it, the cheap orchestrator or the escalated worker? GROOM: retry bound,
    capability-not-model ladder, and owner of the wreckage decision.
R4. Prompt-assembly terms overlap and want a refactor. #7 (skill insertion + episodic
    hits) is now a table-of-contents that #6/#8/#10 flesh out. Make #7 the UMBRELLA
    (prompt assembly), with #8 = skill/KB tier, #6 = episodic tier, #10 = workstream
    tier as its inputs. Reduces the chance a future implementer wires three overlapping
    mechanisms.
R5. Concurrency/ownership story is thin. SKILL is single-writer-per-branch
    ("agent == actor"), but orchestrator wakes, escalation re-dispatch, and parallel
    subtodos introduce races (two wakes racing; a re-dispatch overlapping a still-running
    worker). #2 restartable-stateless helps but is not a lease. GROOM: idempotent
    dispatch + an ownership lease so a re-dispatch cannot double-run an item.
R6. No cost/benefit regime is stated. The entire #8/#9 justification is "lean saves,"
    but never says WHEN. GROOM: a back-of-envelope threshold (stable size x turn count)
    below which you skip retrieval infra and just hand the worker everything. Do not
    build the machine for a regime a fat single agent already wins.
R7. Input observability is missing. #5 captures worker OUTPUTS durably, but when output
    is wrong, "prior not gate" makes the cause SILENT: bad retrieval (#8 missed a
    skill)? wrong coupling seed (#10)? genuine model failure? GROOM: log the ASSEMBLED
    prompt + retrieval hits per dispatch (the #6 episodic index can double as this),
    so failures are attributable, not guesswork.
R8. Human-steering surface vs "review final." The code-review-final insight pushes
    review LATE, but late review of a deep autonomous cascade means expensive rework if
    the WHY drifted EARLY. Tension: catch-drift-early vs review-noise-free-late. GROOM:
    where does the user inspect/steer mid-cascade (cheap checkpoints on WHY/AC) without
    reintroducing per-WorkItem review noise?

BUILD-ORDER OBSERVATION (dependencies, for sequencing WorkItems later)
- #1 (router fields) == 5774 phase 1: the already-valid MVP and foundation.
- #5 (exit contract) is a PREREQUISITE for #6/#8/#10 (they consume its artifacts);
  build it early or the context layer has nothing distilled to seed from.
- #2/#3 (orchestrator + gate) are the runtime spine.
- #6/#8/#9/#10 are one subsystem (context assembly under #7's umbrella) -- design and
  build them together, not as four separate features.

PARTING THOUGHT (reviewer, beyond the point text)
The design is unusually coherent because it keeps rediscovering the SAME invariant from
different angles (ledger-is-the-floor; cache-never-gates) -- that is a good sign. The
risk here is the OPPOSITE of incoherence: it may be OVER-BUILT for its regime (see R6).
Before grooming R1-R8 into WorkItems, settle R6 FIRST -- decide the stable-size x
turn-count threshold at which this whole apparatus beats just handing a capable agent
everything. If that threshold is far from actual usage, several of these points collapse
into "do not bother yet," and the retrospective (and the build) gets much shorter.
Sequencing consequence: R6 is a gate on the rest of grooming, not just another item.
